names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 12 iulie, «Sfânta Veronica», with the rank word left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Ιουλίου, «Αγία Βερονίκη η αιμορροούσα», with the rank word and the description left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 12. јул ст. ст., „Св. Вероника.“ — „Св.“ is not a rank and there is nothing else in the heading, so the bare forename is the whole of what this calendar gives her; «of Caesarea Philippi» in the display name is the corpus’s own and is not in this book at all. `foldchk.py` returns no holder and `sr-foldpred.mjs` predicts a new key with no other holder.

Name page 10120 is «Праведная Вероника» and the day line declines her as «Вероники Палестинской». The bare forename is stored because «Палестинская» stands in the line and not on the name page, and it is the one word this corpus already renders as Caesarea Philippi; `fk.mjs` returns this folder alone for «вероника», the same string already being its Serbian form, so the bare form widens no fold.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 июля ст. ст. — «Прав. Вероники Палестинской (I) Мц. Голиндухи , во св. Крещении Марии (591).»

attestations.note: The day's third entry carries two women on one line and this is the first. Name page 10120 is «Праведная Вероника», which is the `righteous` this folder's `types` already hold, and the line's «(I)» the first century; the folder's Romanian, Greek and Serbian rows all stand on this same menologion day. `dates` unchanged — the folder has none and a Roman numeral would be its first. The line calls her «Палестинская» where the display name has Caesarea Philippi, the city of the woman with the issue of blood, which is in Palestine; no rename. The reading id10120 was NOT opened and the day page prints no hymn under her name.

Nothing on the page connects her with Berenice, daughter of Domnina, whom the corpus keeps; this Veronica is the woman of Caesarea Philippi whom an old tradition identifies with the woman healed of an issue of blood.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Ιουλίου — «Αγία Βερονίκη η αιμορροούσα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and it is plainly the same woman: the woman with the issue of blood of the three Gospels, whom tradition names Veronica, and whom Nicodemus the Hagiorite's synaxarion brings from the city of Paneas — which is Caesarea Philippi, the folder's own byname. She is not the corpus's Berenice, daughter of Domnina. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence, and the page prints no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 25.07.2026 (12. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. Вероника.“

attestations.note: The day’s fourth entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, with its closing full stop, which is what §4 asks for and what `srbody.mjs` now hands back. The identification is a verse of the Gospel and this book gives it: „То је она крвоточна жена, коју је Господ исцелио (Мат. 9, 20)“ — this is that woman with the issue of blood whom the Lord healed — and the Romanian and Greek rows stand on this very 12 July. **`dates` STAY NULL AND THERE IS NOTHING TO REFUSE.** The folder holds no dates; this book gives no year, no century and no reign for her, only „упокојила се мирно“, she reposed peacefully. The one date in the entry belongs to somebody else — the statue was preserved „до времена цара Јулијана Одступника“, until the time of Julian the Apostate — and a reign is no source for a year in any case, least of all for a woman who died two centuries before it. `types` UNTOUCHED at `righteous`: the heading’s only word before the name is „Св.“, which §5 says is not a rank, so **this heading yields no type at all** and the one the folder holds came off another calendar. No `office`, no `locations`. No new `related` rows: the Lord who healed her is not a folder of this corpus, and `nicodemus-the-hagiorite`, whom the folder already relates, is not named here. **WHAT IS NEW IS A STATUE AND A REMARK ABOUT STATUES.** Out of gratitude to her Lord and healer, the Prologue says, Veronica had a statue of the Lord Jesus made, and prayed before it; by tradition that statue was preserved until the time of Julian the Apostate, **who turned it into a statue of the idol Zeus**. And the Prologue adds a remark of its own that is not about her at all: this is one of the rarest cases of statues of saints being used in the Eastern church, whereas, as is known, it later became the general custom of the Western churches. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.
